question: Can a new estimator enter the Technique Graph through a capsule-bound joint-sample contract and demonstrate a statistically resolved equal-cost variance reduction without changing a production route?
hypothesis: For the unit-interval integral of x squared, subtracting the zero-mean control x minus one half with coefficient one reduces replicated sample variance by at least 0.01 while preserving the integral.

inputs.source_identity: HT.4 transport research contract and deterministic host oracle

configuration.metric: replicated sample variance at equal sample cost

reproducibility.seed_policy: Variant and replicate namespaces are derived independently by the HO.2 runner; each invocation uses deterministic splitmix64 counters over disjoint sample ranges.
reproducibility.determinism: The source, manifest, parameter, variant, seed namespace, replicate and sample ranges determine every sample and artifact identity.

baseline: Independent Monte Carlo samples of x squared.
candidate: The same estimator expressed as a ResearchExtension control-variate node with an exact uniform density, sample-mean normalization and known control expectation.

result.conclusion: Eight independent deterministic replicates resolve an equal-cost variance reduction beyond the declared 0.01 threshold, and the assessment becomes eligible for promotion review. The toy domain remains Research evidence and does not establish a scene-rendering speedup.

known_failure_domain: The analytic scalar integral does not establish applicability to a SceneIR workload.
A useful control and its exact expectation are assumed known.
GPU cost, memory, spectral packet behavior and path-space support benefit are not measured.
Promotion still requires the complete HO.2 Research-to-Experimental evidence set.
